name: Cable Front Raise
summary: An isolation exercise that works the anterior deltoids by flexing the shoulders against constant cable resistance.

setup: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable station.
Straddle the cable facing away from the machine, or stand facing it, and grasp the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Step forward slightly to place tension on the cable, standing upright with feet hip-width apart and a soft bend in the knees and elbows.
steps: Brace your core and raise the bar upward in a smooth arc until your hands reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to emphasize peak contraction in the front deltoids.
Lower the bar under control along the same path back to hip level without letting the weight stack touch down.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the bar and inhale as you lower it back down.
cues: Keep elbows softly bent but locked in place

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load and keep your glutes and core tight to isolate the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Raising the bar excessively high above shoulder level.
common_faults.correction: Stop when your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor to keep tension focused on the anterior deltoid.

common_faults.fault: Bending and straightening the elbows during the rep.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a fixed, slight bend in the elbows throughout the entire set.

precautions: Avoid using excessive loads that force hyperextension of the lumbar spine.
